<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 10:14">Targ. Is. X, 14</cite> (ed. Wil. <cite ref="S01534"><he>קִנָה</he></cite>, corr. acc.).
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Judges 14:8">Targ. Jud. XIV, 8</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on I Samuel 14:27">Targ. I Sam. XIV, 27</cite> (h. text <he>יערת</he>); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Chullin 141b:21">Ḥull. 141ᵇ</cite> <he>זיל טרוף אקן וכ׳</he> go and knock at the nest, that the birds be moved, and thus take possession of them.
<cite ref="Gittin 68b:8">Gitt. 68ᵇ</cite> <he>ק׳ דתרנגולא ברא</he> the nest of a woodcock; <he>חפיוה לקִינֵּיה וכ׳</he> they covered his nest with white glass; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 102b:16">Snh. 102ᵇ</cite> (prov.) <he>דפרע קִנְאֵיה מחריב קִינֵּיה</he> Ar. he that wreaks his vengeance destroys his own nest (ed. <he>דפרע קיניה מחריב ביתיה</he>, read with Ms. F. <he>קנאיה</he>).—Pl. <cite ref="S01567"><he>קִנֵּי</he></cite>, <cite ref="S00089"><he>קִי׳</he></cite>.
Erub. 3ᵃ (expl. אמלתרא) ק׳ nest-shaped cornices.—קַן נִשְׁרַיָּיא pr. n. pl. Eagles’ Nest, Ḳan-Nishraya (v. P. Sm. 3673), Kennesrin on the Euphrates.
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 26a:20">R. Hash. 26ᵃ</cite> (Ms. M. <he>קנשרייא</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note).
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 58b">B. Kam. 58ᵇ</cite> <he>תלתא … בק׳ וכ׳</he> three date-trees stood in one place (close together).

<cite ref="Sukkah 32b:19">Succ. 32ᵇ</cite> <he>תלתא תלתא טרפי בק׳</he> three leaves close together (Rashi: on one stem, = <cite ref="S01504"><he>קַן</he></cite>, <cite ref="S01535"><he>קָנֶה</he></cite>).
